Create Synchronized Palette.vi

Owning Palette: VI Helpeks API

The VI creates a palette file synchronized with the given folder. In addition, if allowed, the VI creates a synchronized palette in every sub-folder beneath the given folder recursively.

Details

Click the parameters for details

 

Palette Icon specifies icon of the top-level palette. If Palette Icon is empty picture (by default), the icon is built same way as for sub-palettes (see details in VI description).
Palette File Path specifies path of the top-level palette file which should be created. If the path is empty (by default), the VI creates dir.mnu palette file in the Folder Path folder.
Folder Path specifies a folder, for which the palette is to be created.
Recursively specifies whether to create synchronized palette for every sub-folder. If TRUE, the dir.mnu file is created in every sub-folder and synchronized to it. Default is FALSE.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
Exclude Dir Name pattern specifies sub-folders that should be ignored while creating palettes.  A name pattern is the regular expression for the Match Pattern function. In order to define several patterns, separate them with the Line Feed (i.e. every line contains one pattern). Empty lines are ignored.
Palette File Path out returns the path to the top-level palette file created.
All Palette File Paths returns the paths to all palette files created.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.

 

Create Synchronized Palette details

Palette icons
For the given folder and all sub-folders beneath it (if allowed by <C>Recursively), the VI looks for an image file to use it as icon for the respective palette. A folder's icon file is either of:
(1) A file with the same name as the folder and .png extension that resides in the folder's parent directory.
(2) The dir_icon.png file that resides in the folder.
If neither of these icon file is found, a default icon is set to the respective palette.
Icon of the top-level palette can be defined in the Palette Icon.
